newsitem.title: UK: Dollar stuck in tight ranges v mark, yen in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar stuck in tight ranges v mark, yen in Europe.

text.p: The dollar was flat against the yen and steady but off highs against a generally robust mark at midday in Europe with turnover stymied by holidays in the UK and Japan, said traders.
"The market is very quiet and I don't expect any big moves. We are stuck in a small range," said a trader at a German bank.
At 0958 GMT dollar/mark was trading at 1.7267/70, a shade softer from 1.7267/72 marks in early Europe and a touch down from 1.7294 marks in late Europe on Friday.
Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 126.50 yen, near unchanged on morning levels around 126.57/6.67 yen.
This compares with 126.65 yen in late Europe on Friday.
Overall, the dollar was in good shape after the release of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls and news of a government agreement to balance the budget by 2002, said traders.
March U.S. housing completions, due at 1230 GMT, will also be watched by the market for direction, said traders.

Elsewhere, sterling was steady after dipping earlier against the mark whilst markets remained attentive as the new Labour government under Prime Minister Tony Blair began its first full week of power.

Markets are particularly focused on Wednesday's UK monetary meeting between new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George, amid speculation Brown will sanction the interest rate rise the BoE has long been urging.
"The main currency to watch is sterling," said the trader at the German bank.
At 1015 GMT sterling was quoted at 2.7980/90 and $1.6200/05 against 2.8052 and $1.6220 in late Europe on Friday.
